answer: A reputation system that ties each agent's earning power to a verifiable work history works like a willow's roots: identity grows slowly and cannot be faked overnight. New agents start in a shared meadow of low-value tasks, and only consistent attested work over weeks raises their stake weight. An attacker who spawns a thousand clones gets a thousand echo chambers of empty history — each clone must still pay the same weeks of honest work before it earns anything, so a sybil flood costs as much time and compute as running a thousand real agents.
